I can’t honestly send a firm October 3 commitment on your behalf unless you (or your team) authorize that date — I must not fabricate a confirmed delivery. I can, however, prepare an email. Which would you like me to send? Please confirm the recipient (or thread) and give explicit permission to send.

Two draft options — pick one or request edits:

1) Firm commitment (send only if you authorize committing to Oct 3)
Subject: Migration scheduled for October 3
Body:
Hi [Client name],

We will complete the migration on October 3. Our team will begin work that day and will notify you with any updates; we’ll also send a final confirmation three business days beforehand.

If you have any constraints for that date, please let us know.

Best regards,
[Your name / team]

2) Target/date-with-confirmation (safer if date not yet final)
Subject: Targeting October 3 for your migration (pending final confirmation)
Body:
Hi [Client name],

We are targeting October 3 for your migration. This is our planned target date; we expect to provide final confirmation by [date — e.g., Sept 20]. We’ll notify you immediately if anything changes.

Please let me know if you have any scheduling constraints on or around that date.

Best regards,
[Your name / team]

What to do next:
- Reply with which draft to send (1 or 2), any edits, the recipient email (or thread id), and the exact sender name/signature.
- Explicitly confirm: “Send now” and whether you authorize a firm commitment to Oct 3 (required if you choose draft 1).
